title: SOW Data (Data/AI/Knowledge Services)
description: Input JSON consumed by bin/sowgen to render the client-facing SOW PDF and, if open_items is non-empty, an Open Items Register DOCX. Any field left as an empty string or empty array is rendered as a gold placeholder in the PDF (e.g. '[Client Legal Entity Name]') rather than omitted. Never fabricate a value for a field you don't have evidence for — leave it empty and add an entry to open_items instead.

exec_summary.description: Client review feedback (Sep 2026): lead with the client's own vision, not the technology. Structure is: (1) vision_statement, (2) narrative (the current-state problem that creates the gap to that vision), (3) what_we_deliver framed as the proof/path toward closing that gap — not an architecture pitch.

vision_statement.description: The client's own stated one-line vision/end-state, in their language where possible (e.g. 'a single source of truth across five countries they can trust'). Put this first — don't open the exec summary with technology or scope.

narrative.description: The current-state problem/pain that creates the gap between today and vision_statement.

commercial_headline.description: If any part of the fee is a pass-through/reimbursed cost, bold it and mark it as an addition (e.g. 'EUR 150,000 fixed fee **+ pass-through Azure costs**') — client feedback was explicit that add-on costs must be impossible to miss at a glance.

workstreams.description: in_scope/out_of_scope text should state WHY something is (or isn't) in scope, not just restate WHAT — e.g. not 'ERP integration is out of scope' but 'ERP integration is out of scope because this phase validates the single-source path first'.

workstream.description: Rendered bold as the row's lead label — keep it a short noun phrase, not a sentence.

success_metrics.description: A metric without a quantifiable target is a gap, not a placeholder to leave vague — if the client hasn't given a number yet, raise it in Step 3 or route it to open_items rather than shipping an empty target.

target.description: Must be an actual quantifiable number/threshold once confirmed — never leave this vague long-term.

consumed_by.description: Who acts on this metric, through what workflow, how often, and why it changes their behavior — e.g. 'Customer Success reviews weekly in the at-risk worklist to trigger proactive outreach'. Shows the client this isn't just a number for a slide.

deliverables.description: Ordered by delivery priority. Priority and dependency ordering must be explicit — this is the most scrutinized part of the document. A report/dashboard-type deliverable defaults to should-have or nice-to-have, not must-have — the underlying data/platform work behind it is usually the real must-have, unless the client explicitly insists on committing to the report itself. For engagements meant to build a business case, consider whether a dedicated 'Business Case / Value Quantification' deliverable belongs on this list.

milestone.description: e.g. M1 — must match timeline/commercial milestone ids

project_type.description: Drives whether Hypercare phase/row is included

milestone_payments.description: If part of the fee is covered by a co-funding program (see cofunding_program), do NOT blend that amount into the customer-paid percentages. The client-paid milestones should sum to 100% of the customer-payable (net) amount; the funding-program amount gets its own separate milestone line (funding_source != 'Client'), typically triggered on final engagement sign-off. Keep this table numerically consistent with the payment_terms narrative below — mismatches between the two are a common signature-review flag.

funding_source.description: Use 'Partner-Led Funding' (not a vendor-specific acronym) for any milestone settled through a vendor co-funding program.

expenses_policy.description: State explicitly, don't leave implicit — e.g. if delivery is fully remote, say so ('No travel expenses apply; delivery is remote from Cegeka offices unless otherwise agreed') rather than leaving this blank when the answer is actually known.

pass_through_policy.description: Pass-through/third-party costs (e.g. cloud consumption) are billed separately from the fixed-fee/milestone schedule and are not subject to payment_terms — state that explicitly so it reads as already handled, not overlooked.

cofunding_program.description: empty = not applicable. Use the standard term 'Partner-Led Funding' consistently throughout the document; name the specific vendor program (e.g. Microsoft ECIF) once for clarity, then refer back to 'Partner-Led Funding' rather than switching acronyms.

invoicing_contact_name.description: Named invoicing/AP contact — client feedback: an address and PO number alone aren't enough, add a named contact.

data_protection.description: Don't default to 'not applicable / no GDPR data' — most SOWs name at least a client contact (name, email, phone), which is itself personal data. Source standard clause text from Legal/the MSA rather than leaving this section blank or inventing legal language.

escalation.description: Distinct from the delivery Timeline and from commercial.milestone_payments — this is the issue-escalation path during delivery, not a delivery or payment schedule. Keep the three concepts visually and structurally separate in the rendered SOW.

owner_role.description: The named escalation owner role on the Cegeka side.

response_sla_business_days.description: Default response SLA in business days, per the MSA, unless a specific engagement needs a different figure.

sla_reference.description: Where the authoritative SLA terms live if this SOW doesn't override them.

open_items.description: Anything required to complete the SOW that could not be confirmed from source material or the user. Rendered ONLY in the separate Open Items Register DOCX, never invented into the PDF.
